tag: Yoga, white-water and evening aarti on the Ganga
ab: Rishikesh is where the Ganga leaves the Himalaya: ashrams and yoga schools line both banks, suspension bridges hum with pilgrims, and rafting camps sit upstream at Shivpuri.
ppl: Sadhus in saffron, ashram students in white and Garhwali shopkeepers share the ghats. Mornings begin with chanting and bells, cows wander the bridges, and every evening families float diyas in leaf boats during the aarti. The town is strictly vegetarian and alcohol-free.
go: Jolly Grant (Dehradun) airport 20 km; Yog Nagari Rishikesh railway station

places.d: Hundreds sing as lamps swing over the river at dusk on the ashram's riverfront steps.
The iconic suspension-bridge area with thirteen-storey Trayambakeshwar temple and riverside cafés.
The ruined jungle ashram where the Beatles wrote much of the White Album, now covered in murals.
A 16 km run through grade III rapids like 'Golf Course' and 'Roller Coaster' back into town.
The town's main bathing ghat, said to be where three rivers meet.
A tiered forest waterfall with cool pools, a short walk from the road.
A hilltop shrine where the sun rises over the Garhwal snow peaks.
Jeep safaris for elephants, deer and leopards in the Shivalik forests.

tag: The gateway of the gods, where the Ganga meets the plains
ab: Haridwar is one of Hinduism's seven holiest cities and a host of the Kumbh Mela. The evening aarti at Har Ki Pauri is unforgettable.
ppl: Families come to Haridwar for life's big moments: a child's first haircut, immersing a loved one's ashes, or a dip on a festival day. Pandas, the family priests, still keep handwritten genealogy registers that go back generations; tell them your village and they may find your ancestors.
go: Haridwar Junction railway station; Dehradun airport 35 km

places.d: Thousands of lamps and floating diyas turn the Ganga gold as bells ring at sunset.
places.t: Get a place on the steps by 5 PM.

places.d: A wish-fulfilling goddess temple on Bilwa hill, reached by ropeway.
A hilltop temple across the river with a ropeway and views of the whole city.
The temple where Sati gave up her life, in the old town of Kankhal.
An eight-storey temple to 'Mother India', with a floor for each freedom fighter and saint.
Rudraksha beads, brass lamps and kachoris fried since dawn.

tag: The Queen of the Hills and its quiet cantonment above
ab: Mussoorie's Mall Road buzzes with holidaymakers, while Landour, a few kilometres up, is a calm cantonment of old bakeries, churches and oak forest where Ruskin Bond lives.
ppl: Landour's old families have run the same bakeries and stores since the 1900s, and its Char Dukan corner is everyone's breakfast stop. Below, Jaunsari and Garhwali villagers grow potatoes and rajma on terraces and come up to sell them in the bazaar.
go: Dehradun railway station 35 km; Jolly Grant airport 60 km

places.d: Walk the 'chakkar' loop past St Paul's Church, oak forest and the famous four little shops.
The highest point of Landour, with telescopes trained on Kedarnath and Bandarpunch peaks.
A 3 km car-free promenade with a rock shaped like a camel's hump and sunset views.
A busy waterfall with pools for wading, 15 km from town.
A ropeway ride to Mussoorie's second-highest peak for a view of the Doon valley.
The restored home and lab of the surveyor who mapped the Himalaya, on a windy ridge.
Deodar eco-parks and potato fields on a quiet ridge 25 km away.
The lively promenade of cafés, woollens and evening crowds.

tag: A town around an emerald lake, and quieter lakes beyond
ab: Nainital wraps around a pear-shaped lake under forested peaks. Bhimtal, Sattal and Kainchi Dham, the ashram of Neem Karoli Baba, are close by.
ppl: This is Kumaon. Villagers in nearby hills wear the rangwali pichhaura shawl at weddings, women gather pine needles and fodder in long processions, and Kumaoni holi is sung for weeks in homes. Nainital's boatmen and rickshaw pullers are second- and third-generation.
go: Kathgodam railway station 35 km; Pantnagar airport 70 km

places.d: Row or sail across the lake past the Naina Devi temple and wooded hills.
The goddess temple on the lake's north shore that gave the town its name.
A cable car to a ridge facing Nanda Devi and Trishul on clear mornings.
A 4 km forest walk or pony ride to a rocky lookout over the lake.
Neem Karoli Baba's riverside ashram, a pilgrimage for seekers from around the world.
Quieter lakes in oak forest, with birdwatching and kayaking at Sattal.
An orchard village with a 350-year-old Shiva temple and cliff views to the snow peaks.
The lakeside promenade of bal mithai shops, candle stalls and woollens.

tag: India's first national park, tiger country in sal forest
ab: Corbett was India's first national park and still one of the best places to see a wild tiger, along with elephants, gharials and over 600 bird species. Ramnagar is the base for all zones.
ppl: Van Gujjar buffalo herders once lived inside these forests and still graze at the edges. Naturalists and Gypsy drivers in Ramnagar learned to read tracks from their fathers, and Jim Corbett's own house at Kaladhungi shows how close villagers lived to the big cats.
go: Ramnagar railway station; Pantnagar airport 80 km

places.d: Grassland and sal forest with good tiger sightings; Gypsy safaris run morning and afternoon.
The park's heart on the Ramganga reservoir: elephant herds, tigers and vast chaurs (grasslands).
The zone open all year, good for sloth bears and elephants.
A goddess shrine perched on a rock in the middle of the Kosi river.
A 20 m waterfall in teak forest near Kaladhungi.
Jim Corbett's winter home, with his letters, guns and the village he cared for.

ab: Auli is a slope of oak and meadow above Joshimath with one of India's best ski runs and a direct view of Nanda Devi. In summer it is a flower meadow.
ppl: Garhwali villages around Joshimath keep stone houses with carved wooden doors. Bhotiya traders once carried salt and wool over the passes to Tibet, and families still weave woollen thulmas. Joshimath is the winter seat of Lord Badrinath, carried down each November.
go: Rishikesh 255 km; nearest airport Jolly Grant

places.d: Beginner-friendly ski slopes with instructors, facing Nanda Devi.
A meadow walk through oak forest with views of Trishul and Dronagiri.
A ridge-top lake and chairlift over the slopes with peaks on every side.
The winter home of Lord Badrinath's idol, with an old wooden temple.
A remote forest trail to a small lake below the snowline.

tag: A Jyotirlinga at the foot of the snow, reached on foot
ab: Kedarnath temple stands at 3,583 m beneath the Kedardome peak, a 16 km climb from Gaurikund. It opens from late April or May to just after Diwali.
ppl: Pilgrims of every age make the climb, many carried by Garhwali porters in baskets or on mules. Priests from the Rawal tradition of Karnataka serve the temple, and villages along the way open their homes as rest stops with tea and khichdi.
go: Road to Sonprayag/Gaurikund from Rishikesh (215 km); helicopters from Phata

places.d: The 16 km climb to one of the twelve Jyotirlingas; most pilgrims stay a night at the top.
places.t: Register with the Uttarakhand yatra portal; start before dawn.

places.d: A short climb above Kedarnath to the guardian deity, with a view down the valley.
Where Shiva and Parvati are said to have married; an eternal fire has burned here for ages and couples now marry here too.
A warm spring and Gauri temple where pilgrims bathe before the climb.
A glacial lake above the temple, a steep 3 km hike.

tag: Vishnu's shrine by the Alaknanda and India's first village
ab: Badrinath is one of the Char Dham, a colourful temple by the Alaknanda between Nar and Narayan peaks. Mana, 3 km away, is the first Indian village on the road to Tibet.
ppl: Mana is a Bhotiya village of stone houses where women knit woollens and sell them from their doorsteps, then move down to lower villages for the winter. The temple's chief priest, the Rawal, is always a Namboodiri Brahmin from Kerala, a tradition from Adi Shankaracharya.
go: Road from Rishikesh (300 km) via Joshimath

places.d: A bright painted temple of Lord Badrinarayan, with Tapt Kund hot springs below.
The first village of India: stone lanes, wool shops and the 'last tea shop'.
A natural rock bridge over the roaring Saraswati and the cave where Vyasa dictated the Mahabharata.
A 6 km trail from Mana to a 120 m waterfall dropping from a cliff.
Hot springs below the temple where pilgrims bathe before darshan.

tag: Mini Switzerland: meadows, rhododendron forest and the highest Shiva temple
ab: Chopta is a meadow camp below Tungnath, the world's highest Shiva temple, and Chandrashila peak with a 360° view of Chaukhamba, Nanda Devi and Trishul.
ppl: Villagers from Sari and Makkumath run small dhabas and camps through the season and move down in winter. Shepherds graze sheep on the bugyals, and the Panch Kedar pilgrims have walked these trails for centuries.

places.d: A 3.5 km paved climb to a 1,000-year-old stone temple at 3,680 m.
A further 1.5 km above Tungnath to a summit with the Garhwal Himalaya in a full circle.
A 2.5 km hike from Sari village to a lake that mirrors the Chaukhamba peaks.
A Garhwali farming village of slate-roof homes and homestays.
A small breeding centre for the shy Himalayan musk deer.

tag: A quiet cantonment of pine, oak and old churches
ab: Lansdowne is the home of the Garhwal Rifles, a small cantonment that stayed calm and green while other hill stations grew crowded.
ppl: Almost every Garhwali family has a soldier, and the regiment is a matter of pride here. Village women carry fodder and firewood up steep paths, and the market closes early, so life follows the bugle and the sun.

places.d: A cliff-edge point with the snow peaks of the Garhwal range on clear days.
A small lake built by the Army, with paddle boats and ducks.
Medals, uniforms and stories of the regiment's two Victoria Cross winners.
A 1895 stone church, now a small museum of old photographs.
A Shiva temple in a dense deodar forest 35 km away, cool and silent.

tag: Seven cities of history, one great street-food capital
ab: Delhi has been the capital of empires for a thousand years: Mughal forts and tombs, a Sultanate minaret, Lutyens' boulevards and the lanes of Old Delhi, all in one sprawling city.
ppl: Delhi is a city of migrants: Punjabi families who came after Partition, Bihari workers, Bengalis in Chittaranjan Park, Tibetans in Majnu ka Tilla. Old Delhi still lives in havelis where families have run the same sweet or spice shop for five generations, and every Delhiite has an opinion on the best chhole bhature.
go: Indira Gandhi International Airport; New Delhi railway station

places.d: Shah Jahan's red sandstone palace-fort, from where the Prime Minister speaks on Independence Day.
India's largest mosque, with a minaret climb over the rooftops of Old Delhi.
places.t: Closed to visitors during prayer times.

places.d: Paranthe Wali Gali, Jalebi Wala, kachoris and lassi in kulhads in Mughal-era lanes.
The garden tomb that inspired the Taj Mahal, beautifully restored.
A 73 m fluted tower from 1193 with an iron pillar that has not rusted in 1,600 years.
Over 100 monuments, stepwells and tombs scattered through a wild park beside the Qutub.
The war memorial arch and boulevard, best in the evening when families come out for ice cream.
A gold-domed Sikh shrine with a holy pool and a langar that feeds thousands every day.
A vast carved pink-sandstone temple with an evening water show.
A Bahá'í house of worship shaped like a marble lotus, open to all faiths for silent prayer.
15th-century tombs among lawns where Delhi jogs, picnics and does yoga.
A restored Mughal garden of tombs, lotus ponds and birds next to Humayun's Tomb.
A 108-step stepwell hidden between office towers near Connaught Place.
Medieval madrasa ruins over a lake, surrounded by cafés, bars and boutiques.
Harappan seals, Chola bronzes and Buddhist relics: 5,000 years of India in one building.

tag: The Taj Mahal and the Mughal capital around it
ab: Agra was the Mughal capital before Delhi. Beyond the Taj Mahal, it holds the red fort-palace of Akbar, the jewel-box Baby Taj and the abandoned city of Fatehpur Sikri.
ppl: Many Agra families are descendants of the artisans who built the Taj: marble inlayers in the Tajganj lanes still set carnelian and lapis into white stone by hand, using techniques passed from father to son. Petha sweet-makers, rickshaw-wallahs and carpet weavers fill the old city around them.
go: Agra Cantt railway station (Gatimaan from Delhi in 1 hr 40 min); Agra airport

places.d: Shah Jahan's white marble tomb for Mumtaz Mahal, rose-pink at sunrise and gold at sunset.
places.t: Go at sunrise; fee includes the main mausoleum. Closed Fridays.

places.d: Akbar's red sandstone fort where Shah Jahan spent his last years looking at the Taj.
The moonlight garden across the Yamuna, with the Taj reflected at sunset and no crowds.
A small tomb covered in delicate pietra dura that came before the Taj.
Akbar's red sandstone city, abandoned after 14 years, with the great Buland Darwaza.
Akbar's tomb in a deer-filled garden, mixing Hindu, Islamic and Jain design.
Old Agra's market for wedding finery, spices and the famous petha sweet.
Watch artisans descended from the Taj's builders cut and set stones into marble by hand.

tag: The oldest living city, on the steps of the Ganga
ab: Varanasi has been continuously inhabited for 3,000 years. Its 84 ghats run along the Ganga, where life and death, worship and washing all happen in plain sight.
ppl: Banarasis start the day with a dip, a paan and a cup of tea on the ghats. Wrestlers train in akharas, Mallah boatmen have rowed these waters for generations, and in Madanpura the clack of handlooms weaving Banarasi silk saris never stops. Families bring their elders here, believing that dying in Kashi brings liberation.
go: Lal Bahadur Shastri airport 25 km; Varanasi Junction

places.d: Seven priests swing great brass lamps in unison as conch shells sound over the river.
places.t: Watch from a boat for the best view.

places.n: Sunrise boat ride along the ghats
places.d: Drift past bathers, yogis and smoking pyres as the sun comes up over the far bank.
The golden Jyotirlinga temple, now reached by the wide Kashi Vishwanath corridor from the river.
places.t: Phones and bags must be deposited.

places.d: Where the Buddha gave his first sermon, with the Dhamek Stupa and the Ashokan lion capital museum.
The southern ghat with a dawn aarti, music and yoga, and cafés above the steps.
The main cremation ghat, where fires have burned without stopping for centuries; observe quietly and do not photograph.
Kachoris, jalebis and lassi in lanes too narrow for cars, between temples and cows.
Visit a family handloom where one sari can take weeks of weaving gold-thread brocade.
The 18th-century riverside fort of the Maharaja of Benares, with vintage cars and old clocks.
A tall marble temple on the leafy campus of Banaras Hindu University.

tag: Lord Ram's city on the Saryu
ab: Ayodhya is revered as Lord Ram's birthplace. The new Ram Mandir opened in 2024, and the city's ghats, temples and lanes now draw pilgrims from all over the world.
ppl: Ayodhya's sadhus and akharas follow ancient Vaishnav traditions, and Ramayana recitals echo from small temples every evening. At Deepotsav on Diwali eve, lakhs of diyas are lit on the Saryu ghats by volunteers, a festival the whole town prepares for.
go: Ayodhya Dham Junction; Maharishi Valmiki airport

places.d: The new Nagara-style temple of pink sandstone with an idol of Ram Lalla.
places.t: Phones and bags are not allowed; use the free lockers.

places.d: A fortress-like Hanuman temple up 76 steps; tradition says visit here first.
A chain of riverside ghats lit with lamps for the evening aarti.
A palace-temple said to be Kaikeyi's gift to Sita, with gold-crowned idols.
A quiet riverside ghat where Ram is said to have taken jal samadhi.

tag: Krishna's childhood land of temples and Holi colours
ab: Mathura is Krishna's birthplace and Vrindavan the forest of his youth: thousands of temples, ghats on the Yamuna, and the most joyful Holi in India at Barsana and Nandgaon.
ppl: Braj is a land of song. Widows in white find shelter in ashrams and sing bhajans all day, families greet each other with 'Radhe Radhe' instead of hello, and at Holi the women of Barsana chase the men of Nandgaon with sticks in the famous Lathmar Holi.
go: Mathura Junction; 3 hours from Delhi on the Yamuna Expressway

places.d: Vrindavan's most loved temple, where curtains are drawn every few minutes so devotees can't stare too long at Krishna.
A white marble temple whose carvings light up in changing colours each evening.
The Krishna-Balaram temple, full of kirtan and dancing devotees.
The temple complex built over the prison cell where Krishna was born.
Mathura's main ghat, where Krishna rested after defeating Kansa; lamps float down the Yamuna at dusk.
Pilgrims walk the 21 km parikrama of the hill Krishna lifted on his finger.
Radha's village with the hilltop Shriji temple, heart of Lathmar Holi.
A grove of twisted tulsi trees where Krishna is believed to dance the raas each night.

tag: The city of Nawabs, kababs and chikankari
ab: Lucknow was the capital of the Nawabs of Awadh, whose taste for poetry, architecture and food still shapes the city: grand imambaras, a famous labyrinth, and kababs so soft they melt.
ppl: Lucknowis are famous for tehzeeb, a courtly politeness: 'pehle aap' (after you). Women embroider delicate chikankari by hand in old-city homes, and the evening walk through Aminabad or Chowk ends with kababs, kulfi and paan.
go: Chaudhary Charan Singh airport; Lucknow Charbagh station

places.d: A vast vaulted hall without a single beam, and a maze of 1,000 passages on the roof.
The 'palace of lights', filled with Belgian chandeliers.
A 60 m Awadhi gateway, the symbol of the city.
Cannon-scarred ruins from the 1857 siege, now a quiet park.
Tunday Kababi, Idris biryani, Prakash kulfi and chikankari shops in the old city.
Watch women stitch the shadow-work embroidery Lucknow is famous for.
A massive park of pink stone and elephant statues, lit up at night.

tag: Where three rivers meet and the Kumbh gathers the world
ab: Prayagraj stands at the Triveni Sangam, the meeting of the Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati, host of the Kumbh Mela. It was also a centre of India's freedom movement.
ppl: Every January, the Magh Mela turns the sandbanks into a tent city of kalpvasis who live by the river for a month of prayer. Boatmen ferry pilgrims to the exact meeting point of the rivers, and the city's old families have strong ties to Nehru-era politics and Hindi literature.

places.d: Row out to where the muddy Ganga meets the green Yamuna for a holy dip.
The Nehru family home, a centre of the freedom struggle.
A reclining Hanuman idol near the Sangam, said to be bathed by the Ganga each monsoon.
Three Mughal tombs in a walled garden, including Jahangir's rebel son Khusrau.
A grand 1887 Gothic cathedral known as the 'Patthar Girja'.

tag: The Golden Temple, the border ceremony and Punjab's best food
ab: Amritsar is the spiritual home of the Sikhs, built around the Golden Temple. Jallianwala Bagh and the Wagah border ceremony tell the story of Partition and freedom.
ppl: Seva, selfless service, is everywhere: volunteers of every background cook and serve free langar to around 100,000 people a day at the Golden Temple and wash every plate by hand. Punjabi warmth means you'll be offered lassi in steel glasses big enough to be a meal.
go: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport; Amritsar Junction

places.d: The gold-covered shrine in a holy pool, with hymns sung from 3 AM until late at night.
places.t: Cover your head, remove shoes, and eat at the langar.

places.d: The garden where British troops fired on a peaceful crowd in 1919; bullet marks remain.
The daily flag-lowering ceremony of high kicks and patriotic roars at the India–Pakistan border.
places.t: Reach by 3:30 PM for a seat.

places.d: Letters, objects and voices of the families torn apart in 1947, in the old Town Hall.
A restored 18th-century fort with a light show and Punjabi food stalls.
A Hindu temple in a sacred tank, built in the style of the Golden Temple.
Crispy Amritsari kulchas at Kulcha Land, lassi at Gian di Lassi, phirni in clay pots.

tag: Le Corbusier's planned city and a garden made of junk
ab: India's first planned city, designed by Le Corbusier, with tree-lined sectors, a lake under the Shivaliks and a UNESCO-listed Capitol Complex.
ppl: Chandigarh was built for families displaced by Partition, and it still feels orderly and green. Evenings mean a walk by Sukhna Lake, and Nek Chand, a road inspector, secretly built a fantasy garden from broken tiles and bangles that became the Rock Garden.

places.d: Nek Chand's secret kingdom of figures made from waste, waterfalls and twisting paths.
A lake at the foot of the Shivaliks for boating and evening walks.
Le Corbusier's concrete assembly, high court and Open Hand monument; free guided tours.
Asia's largest rose garden, with 1,600 varieties.
